name: Binary Numbers AND Sum
description: You are given two huge binary integer numbers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ of lengths $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ respectively. You will repeat the following process: if $$$b \gt 0$$$, then add to the answer the value $$$a~ \&~ b$$$ and divide $$$b$$$ by $$$2$$$ rounding down (i.e. remove the last digit of $$$b$$$), and repeat the process again, otherwise stop the process. The value $$$a~ \&~ b$$$ means bitwise AND of $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. Your task is to calculate the answer modulo $$$998244353$$$. Note that you should add the value $$$a~ \&~ b$$$ to the answer in decimal notation, not in binary. So your task is to calculate the answer in decimal notation. For example, if $$$a = 1010_2~ (10_{10})$$$ and $$$b = 1000_2~ (8_{10})$$$, then the value $$$a~ \&~ b$$$ will be equal to $$$8$$$, not to $$$1000$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$ and the length of $$$b$$$ correspondingly. The second line of the input contains one huge integer $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that this number consists of exactly $$$n$$$ zeroes and ones and the first digit is always $$$1$$$. The third line of the input contains one huge integer $$$b$$$. It is guaranteed that this number consists of exactly $$$m$$$ zeroes and ones and the first digit is always $$$1$$$.
output_specification: Print the answer to this problem in decimal notation modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.
